claude.ts.label: Claude
claude.ts.summary: Send a prompt to Claude and get a single-turn text response back.
claude.ts.description: Send a prompt to Claude and get a response back — summarise upstream text, classify inputs, or generate responses. The graph itself is your agent loop.

inputs.label: Optional user message text (overrides params.messages if set)

prompt.description: Single user message (used when no 'prompt' input and no params.messages).

messages.description: Full conversation history ({role, content}); overrides params.prompt.

examples.title: One-shot summary

params.prompt: Summarize the upstream text in one sentence.

examples.notes: Wire the text to summarise into the 'prompt' input; params.prompt is the instruction.

params.prompt: Your bank account has been compromised

excel_read.ts.label: Excel: read
excel_read.ts.summary: Read rows from an .xlsx workbook in the workspace; the first row is the headers by default.
excel_read.ts.description: Read an .xlsx workbook from the workspace into a row stream. The first row becomes the object keys (headers) unless headers:false. Restrict to a cell range (e.g. "A1:D100") or skip leading rows; flip on typed mode for native numbers/dates/booleans instead of strings.

path.description: Workspace-relative path to the .xlsx. Ignored if a 'path' input is wired.

sheet.description: Sheet name; defaults to the first sheet.

headers.description: Treat the first row as headers (default true). False → rows are arrays.

skip.description: Skip this many leading rows before reading.

typed.description: Return native numbers/dates/booleans instead of strings.

excel_write.ts.label: Excel: write
excel_write.ts.summary: Serialize a row stream into an .xlsx workbook in the workspace, optionally appending to an existing sheet.
excel_write.ts.description: Write a row stream (array of objects) to an .xlsx workbook in the workspace. Wire a 'headers' input to fix column order; otherwise columns are derived from the first row. With append:true, rows are added to an existing sheet of the same name. (autosize/freezeRow are accepted for compatibility but not applied — SheetJS has no styling.)

append.description: Append rows to an existing sheet of the same name instead of overwriting.

autosize.description: Accepted for compatibility; not applied (no styling).

freezeRow.description: Accepted for compatibility; not applied (no styling).

github_add_comment.ts.label: GitHub add comment
github_add_comment.ts.summary: Post a Markdown comment to a GitHub issue or pull request via the REST API.
github_add_comment.ts.description: Add a comment to a GitHub issue or pull request. Works for both — GitHub treats them as the same under the hood. The body supports Markdown and can come from the 'body' input or params.

issue_number.description: Issue OR PR number (shared number space).

body.description: Comment body. Overridden by the 'body' input port.

github_create_issue.ts.label: GitHub create issue
github_create_issue.ts.summary: Open a new GitHub issue on a repo with optional labels, assignees, and milestone.
github_create_issue.ts.description: Open a new issue on a GitHub repo. The body supports Markdown and can come from the 'body' input or params.

body.description: Issue body (Markdown). Overridden by the 'body' input.

examples.title: Triage issue with labels and assignee

github_list_issues.ts.label: GitHub list issues
github_list_issues.ts.summary: Query a repo's issues with filters for state, labels, assignee, and an updated-since cutoff.
github_list_issues.ts.description: List issues on a GitHub repo with optional filters (state, labels, assignee, since-date). Heads-up: pull requests also come back from this endpoint.

since.description: RFC3339 timestamp; only issues updated after this.

examples.title: Open bugs assigned to a teammate

gmail_get_message.ts.label: Gmail get message
gmail_get_message.ts.summary: Fetch a single Gmail message by ID and return its headers, snippet, and decoded body text.
gmail_get_message.ts.description: Fetch one Gmail message by ID. Outputs the common headers (from, to, subject, date), a short snippet, and the plain-text/HTML body when present. Typically used after the search drop with a for_each to expand IDs into full messages.

base_url.description: Override the API host (proxy / self-hosted / testing).

format.description: How much of the message to fetch.

examples.title: Full message body for an ID from search

gmail_search_messages.ts.label: Gmail search messages
gmail_search_messages.ts.summary: Search the connected Gmail mailbox with Gmail query syntax and return matching message IDs.
gmail_search_messages.ts.description: Search your Gmail inbox using normal Gmail search syntax (e.g. `is:unread newer_than:5m label:invoices`). Returns message IDs — pair with gmail_get_message in a for_each to fetch full content.

base_url.description: Override the API host (proxy / self-hosted / testing).

page_token.description: Cursor for the next page (from a previous run's next_page_token).

examples.title: Alert emails from a known sender
examples.notes: Pairs cleanly with a poll_trigger using newer_than as the window.

gmail_send_email.ts.label: Gmail send email
gmail_send_email.ts.summary: Send an email through the user's connected Gmail account, in plain text or HTML, with optional attachments and threading.
gmail_send_email.ts.description: Send an email through your connected Gmail account. The body comes from the 'body' input or the 'body' param; set format to html for rich content. Wire any number of file-producing nodes into the variadic 'attachments' input to attach files — each ref's MIME + filename ride through to the recipient. The 'from' address is fixed to your authorized Google account.

inputs.label: Files to attach (wire zero or more file-producing nodes)

base_url.description: Override the API host (proxy / self-hosted / testing).

body.description: Default body when the input port isn't wired.

thread_id.description: Gmail thread ID to thread this reply into.

examples.title: Daily report with a PDF attachment
examples.notes: Wire a file-producing node (e.g. sheets_export_pdf) into the variadic 'attachments' input.

notion_create_page.ts.label: Notion create page
notion_create_page.ts.summary: Create a Notion page as either a database row or a child of another page, with optional block content.
notion_create_page.ts.description: Create a Notion page. Set the parent (a database → the page becomes a row, or a page → a child). Properties define field values; optional child blocks fill the body. Wire upstream text into 'content' to append paragraph blocks.

requiresConnections.name: NOTION_TOKEN
requiresConnections.note: Notion integration token (or connect via OAuth).

inputs.label: Body text appended as paragraph block(s) (optional)

outputs.label: Web URL of the new page

parent_database_id.description: Parent database UUID. Mutually exclusive with parent_page_id.

parent_page_id.description: Parent page UUID. Mutually exclusive with parent_database_id.

examples.title: Add a row to a tasks database

notion_query_database.ts.label: Notion query database
notion_query_database.ts.summary: Fetch a page of Notion database rows by filter and sort, returning the page objects plus pagination cursor.
notion_query_database.ts.description: Query a Notion database with optional filters and sorting. Page objects come back raw; a downstream compute_rows extracts the properties you care about. Cursor outputs support polling.

requiresConnections.name: NOTION_TOKEN
requiresConnections.note: Notion integration token (or connect via OAuth).

outputs.label: Cursor for the next page (empty when done)

database_id.description: UUID of the database to query.

start_cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a prior call's next_cursor.

ntfy.ts.label: ntfy
ntfy.ts.summary: Publish a push notification to an ntfy topic with optional title, priority, tags, click-URL, and bearer token.
ntfy.ts.description: Push a notification through ntfy.sh (or a self-hosted ntfy server). Set the server, topic, and message; optional title, priority, tags, and click-URL attach extras.

message.description: Notification body. Overridden by the 'body' input.

tags.description: Emoji shortcodes or words shown next to the title.

click.description: URL to open when the notification is tapped.

examples.title: Simple message to a public topic
High-priority alert on a self-hosted server

sheets_append_row.ts.label: Sheets append rows
sheets_append_row.ts.summary: Append rows to a Google Sheet tab, with the first row picking column order from headers.
sheets_append_row.ts.description: Append rows to a Google Sheet. Rows come in on the 'rows' input; column order is the optional 'headers' input or derived (sorted) from row keys.

base_url.description: Override the API host (proxy / self-hosted / testing).

range.description: Sheet name or range; appends after the last populated row.

examples.title: Append to the default sheet
examples.notes: Rows come in on the 'rows' input port.

sheets_export_pdf.ts.label: Sheets export PDF
sheets_export_pdf.ts.summary: Export a Google Sheet to a PDF in the workspace sandbox, ready to attach to an email.
sheets_export_pdf.ts.description: Render a Google Sheet as a PDF and stash it in the run's sandbox so a downstream node (typically gmail_send_email's attachments port) can pick it up.

base_url.description: Override the API host (proxy / self-hosted / testing).

examples.title: Daily report into scratch for gmail_send_email
examples.notes: Wire the 'pdf' output into gmail_send_email's 'attachments' port.

sheets_read_range.ts.label: Sheets read range
sheets_read_range.ts.summary: Read a tab or A1 range from a Google Sheet into rows + headers for downstream drops.
sheets_read_range.ts.description: Read a range from a Google Sheet into rows. The first row becomes the headers by default (override with headers=false for synthetic col_0/col_1 names).

base_url.description: Override the API host (proxy / self-hosted / testing).

spreadsheet_id.description: Sheet ID or full URL (the ID is extracted).

headers.description: When true, the first row is treated as column headers.

slack_list_channels.ts.label: Slack list channels
slack_list_channels.ts.summary: List the Slack channels the connected bot can see, optionally filtered by channel type.
slack_list_channels.ts.description: List the channels your Slack bot can see. Useful for filling a channel picker, or for flows that fan out to every matching channel.

base_url.description: Override the API host (proxy / self-hosted / testing).

types.description: Comma-separated channel types: public_channel, private_channel, mpim, im.

examples.title: DMs and group DMs only
examples.notes: Fan out alerts to every direct conversation the bot is in.

slack_send_message.ts.label: Slack send message
slack_send_message.ts.summary: Post a message to a Slack channel as the connected bot, with optional thread_ts and Block Kit.
slack_send_message.ts.description: Post a message to a Slack channel. The simplest path: set the channel and either type your message in 'text' or wire upstream text into the 'body' input. For richer formatting — buttons, dividers, images — use Block Kit blocks instead of plain text.

inputs.label: Block Kit array (overrides params.blocks; text becomes the push-notification fallback)

base_url.description: Override the API host (proxy / self-hosted / testing).

account.description: Name of the connected Slack workspace.

channel.description: Channel ID (C123) or name (#data-ops). Bot must already be a member.

thread_ts.description: Parent message timestamp to reply in thread.

blocks.description: Block Kit elements; overrides text rendering for rich messages.

examples.title: Threaded reply by channel ID
examples.notes: Use the channel ID (Cxxx) for DMs and private channels; #name works for public ones.

examples.title: Block Kit message with a fallback text
examples.notes: When blocks are set, text is used only as the push-notification fallback.

webhook_send.ts.label: Webhook send
webhook_send.ts.summary: POST/PUT/PATCH a payload to a webhook URL, auto-JSON-marshaling non-string bodies and surfacing non-2xx as errors.
webhook_send.ts.description: Send a payload to any webhook URL — Slack, Discord, Teams, PagerDuty, or a custom receiver. Body can come from an upstream node (objects auto-convert to JSON) or params.

url.description: Full webhook URL. Use ${secret:NAME} to avoid embedding credentials.

body.description: Default body when no input is wired. Strings sent as-is; anything else JSON-marshaled.

content_type.description: Content-Type for string bodies (objects force application/json).
